=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:
  SPA-N-001: General liability cap
  SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
  SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
  SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Baseline:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics; AUD 24,000,000; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law

## Preliminary point: the Seller's "market context" preamble

The preamble says the positions are "market standard", were "settled at principal level by both deal teams" and are "FINAL and not intended to be re-opened". This is the Seller's advocacy, not an agreed position.

- **Before relying on it,** Wattlebridge principals should confirm internally whether any of these points were actually agreed.
- **Absent a signed term sheet saying otherwise,** every point below is open for mark-up.
- **Even if some economics were agreed,** the draft mechanics (disclosure, knowledge, category collapse) go well beyond headline economics.

The Disclosure Letter itself confirms most of the critical deal-specific issues remain unresolved (paras 2–6, 8, 10).

## Liability Regime

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** Cap of 20% of price (AUD 4.8m), applied to all Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** A higher general warranty cap (counter 40–50%, around AUD 9.6–12m). Fundamental, title, tax and specific indemnities should sit outside this cap, capped at 100% of price. Fraud should be uncapped.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter.** Consider landing at 25–30% only if all carve-outs are conceded. *Reason: 20% is defensible only for pure general warranties. Applied to all Claims, it caps exposure on known, quantifiable risks (Bluefen, Ironquay, privacy) well below potential loss.*

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000 per claim. Deductible basket AUD 250,000 (about 1.04%), with only the excess recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - De minimis around AUD 10,000.
  - Basket around AUD 120,000 (0.5%), structured as a **tipping basket** (first-dollar recovery once exceeded).
  - Related claims aggregated for the de minimis.
  - Neither threshold to apply to fundamental, tax or indemnity claims.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as drafted; counter.** *Reason: a 1% deductible plus a high de minimis wipes out mid-sized claims in a AUD 24m SaaS deal. Related-claim aggregation stops the Seller from splitting claims below the threshold, as appears to have happened with the Sandbar contracts.*

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion. Under clause 12.3/13, the same limit applies to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **General warranties:** 24 months, covering two full audit cycles.
  - **Fundamental/title:** 6–7 years.
  - **Tax:** the statutory amendment period plus 6 months.
  - **Specific indemnities:** at least 3 years, or the relevant limitation period.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter at 24 months and reject the "applies to all Claims" default.** *Reason: 18 months may not cover a full post-Completion audit. Applying it to every claim type silently truncates tax and title protection.*

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Capacity, authority, title, share capital and solvency warranties capped at 100% of price, with a 6–7 year time limit. No de minimis or basket. Not qualified by disclosure or Buyer knowledge.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** *Reason: if title fails, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing. A 20% cap on that warranty is not a simplification but a transfer of the core deal risk.*

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature". There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out removing all limitations, the exclusive-remedy clause and the non-reliance clause for fraud, dishonesty or wilful concealment by the Seller, the Company or their officers and advisers. Statutory rights for misleading or deceptive conduct (ACL s18) should also be preserved, to the extent they cannot be excluded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject and insert the express carve-out.** *Reason: courts are reluctant to let parties contract out of their own fraud, but the Buyer should not have to litigate the point. Non-reliance clauses can otherwise weaken ACL claims.*

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** One limitation regime governs every Claim (clauses 12.3/13 and 9.3/12.8/20.5) unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate, express regimes for each category:
  - general warranties;
  - fundamental/title warranties;
  - tax (warranties plus a tax indemnity or deed);
  - specific indemnities (Ironquay, privacy incident, bonuses and on-costs, Sandbar, Riverlark leakage);
  - leakage/price adjustment;
  - fraud.

  The default should be reversed: limitations apply **only** to general warranty claims unless expressly extended.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the default and restructure.** *Reason: this is the most consequential drafting point. As drafted, the general cap, basket, time limit, disclosure and knowledge qualifiers would neutralise every specific protection negotiated elsewhere.*

## Disclosure and Knowledge

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" (DL 1.1–1.2). Para 1.4 also disclaims any admission of materiality or liability.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Only **specific disclosures** in the Disclosure Letter, made fairly, with enough detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely impact, cross-referenced to the relevant warranty.
  - No general data room disclosure. At most, limited public searches (ASIC, PPSR, court searches) on a named date.
  - Disclosure not to qualify fundamental warranties, tax or indemnities.
  - A frozen data room index (USB) to be annexed.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject general disclosure.** *Reason: data room-wide disclosure converts the warranties into the Buyer's own due diligence risk. It would disclose away exactly the issues the Seller admits are unresolved.*

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter known to the Buyer **or its advisers**, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (clause 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** A pro-sandbagging clause: Buyer knowledge, actual or constructive, does not reduce any claim. As a fallback, limit the qualifier to the actual knowledge of named Wattlebridge deal team members, carving out indemnities, fundamental and tax claims.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; insert pro-sandbagging.** *Reason: "advisers" plus "discoverable" imputes the entire due diligence record. Every red flag we have raised would become non-claimable.*

## Conditions, Completion and Funds Flow

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** The Seller uses reasonable endeavours, and the condition is treated as satisfied once the counterparty delivers written consent. DL 2 confirms no final consent, and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A **condition precedent** in the Buyer's favour, which only the Buyer can waive.
  - The condition satisfied only by an unconditional (or Buyer-approved conditional) written consent under DD-002 clause 11.2, plus evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are met.
  - "All reasonable endeavours" by the Seller, with a Buyer right to review consent wording.
  - A sunset date with a walk right.
  - Optionally, a price adjustment or escrow if the consent carries adverse terms.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the Seller mechanism.** *Reason: Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (about AUD 3.6m). A conditional consent the Seller can unilaterally deem "satisfied" leaves the Buyer exposed to termination or repricing after Completion.*

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Release of the facility (about AUD 3.2m) to be provided **after** Completion. DL 3 confirms it is not repaid and no discharge is in hand.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The full payout figure, including interest and break costs, treated as Indebtedness and paid at Completion from the purchase price through the funds flow.
  - A signed payout letter before Completion, and a deed of release plus PPSR discharges (including any share security) delivered **at** Completion.
  - A specific indemnity for any residual amounts.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** *Reason: the deal is debt-free/cash-free. Change of control under DD-003 clause 8.1 may trigger default, and post-Completion release leaves security over an asset the Buyer has paid for.*

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 in DD-005 Completion bonuses is "a matter for the Seller" and is not itemised in the funds flow. DL 5 is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Bonuses plus all employer on-costs (payroll tax, super guarantee, workers' comp, PAYG compliance) defined as Transaction Expenses or Indebtedness and deducted from the price.
  - Payment through Company payroll at or immediately after Completion, funded by the Seller.
  - A specific indemnity, outside the cap and basket, covering amounts that crystallise later under the continued-employment conditions.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the Seller position; require a price deduction plus an indemnity.** *Reason: the Company, not the Seller, is the legal payer. Without a funds-flow line item, the Buyer effectively pays at least about AUD 420k extra after the price is settled.*

## Specific Risks

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The existing indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment (DD-010: AUD 180,000 open) and is "considered adequate". DL 4 confirms no proof of payment and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **As a CP or Completion deliverable:** evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees, plus a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay (and moral rights consents where relevant).
  - **A broad specific indemnity** covering third-party IP claims, the loss of or inability to use the SOW3 Project Materials, and remediation and re-development costs. This should sit outside the cap, basket and disclosure, with a time limit of at least 3–6 years.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as inadequate.** *Reason: under DD-004 clause 7.3, title to the Project Materials does not pass until every fee is paid. The risk is losing core product IP, not a AUD 180k debt.*

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material. DL 6 discloses about 1,240 records sent by link to an unintended external address, with access, scope and notifiability all unresolved.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Pre-Completion covenants:**
    - complete the eligible-data-breach assessment under the Privacy Act Notifiable Data Breaches scheme;
    - obtain an independent forensic report, including link access logs and revocation;
    - make any required OAIC and individual notifications;
    - share all correspondence with the Buyer.
  - **A specific indemnity** for regulatory penalties, notification and remediation costs, third-party claims and customer credits. This should sit outside the cap, basket, disclosure and knowledge qualifiers, ideally backed by an escrow or retention.
  - Warranty that no other incidents have occurred.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "not material" characterisation; require an indemnity plus covenants.** *Reason: the Act generally expects assessment within 30 days. The matter was still "preliminary" at 22 September and it is now November, which itself creates compliance exposure. The penalty regime has been significantly increased.*

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 total) are "ordinary-course operating costs". DL 8 says to read DD-008 and DD-011 together, and does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Full copies of the renewals, plus confirmation of approval authority and any internal thresholds.
  - Treatment as non-ordinary course requiring Buyer consent under the conduct-of-business clause.
  - If they were entered without that consent, or are not terminable without cost: either (a) termination before Completion at the Seller's cost, or (b) treatment as Leakage or debt-like items deducted from the price, or covered by a specific indemnity.
  - Related-party and contract-splitting warranties.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the "ordinary course" label; investigate and reserve.** *Reason: three identical AUD 110k related renewals look like a single AUD 330k commitment split to stay under an approval or disclosure threshold.*

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced" by the share register at DD-012. DL 10 itself notes the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Buyer-side verification: current ASIC company extract and historical share issues, constitution, all issue and transfer documents, share certificates, a PPSR search over the shares, and a check for options, convertibles, ESOP or other rights to shares.
  - A warranty of 100% legal and beneficial title free of Encumbrances, under the fundamental regime in SPA-N-004.
  - **At Completion:** signed transfers, original certificates (or a lost-certificate indemnity), resignations, and releases of any security over the shares (link to Riverlark).
- **Recommendation:** **Do not rely on the register alone.** *Reason: a share register is only prima facie evidence. Riverlark security or unrecorded equity rights could defeat 100% title.*

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP positions are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Tax:** a separate tax indemnity or deed covering pre-Completion tax (including payroll tax and super on the bonuses), with Buyer conduct of tax claims, outside the general cap and basket, running for the statutory period plus 6 months.
  - **IP:** detailed IP warranties covering ownership and assignments from employees and contractors (including Ironquay), open-source compliance, no infringement, and data and privacy compliance. Title-to-IP elements should be treated as quasi-fundamental.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "settled"; table full tax and IP terms in our mark-up.** *Reason: in a SaaS acquisition, tax and IP are core value drivers. Folding them into a 20% / 18-month / data room-disclosed regime leaves them effectively unprotected.*

## Other Points (Not Itemised Above)

- **Office lease (DD-007):** Confirm the notification obligation is given at or before Completion, and the Seller warrants that no landlord consent is required.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** Obtain legal confirmation that the assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale or change of control. If uncertain, seek a comfort letter.
- **DL 1.4 non-admission and DL 11 reservation:** Acceptable as non-admissions only. Ensure they do not dilute specific disclosure standards or indemnities.

## Suggested Next Steps

1. **Confirm internally** whether any principal-level agreement exists on cap, basket or time limits.
2. **Issue the Buyer mark-up,** leading with category separation (N-014), disclosure (N-006) and knowledge (N-007), since these determine whether every other protection works.
3. **Send a supplementary due diligence request** covering Bluefen consent drafts, the Riverlark payout figure, Ironquay payment evidence, the privacy forensic status, Sandbar contracts and title documents.
4. **If W&I insurance is contemplated,** align the policy exclusions so the known matters (N-008 to N-013) are covered by Seller indemnities or escrow, since W&I insurers will exclude known issues.

*This is a working analysis for the Buyer deal team and should be reviewed by supervising NSW counsel before it is sent to the Seller.*

- **Recommendation:** **Reject the Seller mechanism.** *Reason: Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (about AUD 3.6m). A conditional consent the Seller can unilaterally deem "satisfied" leaves the Buyer exposed to termination or repricing after Completion.*

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Release of the facility (about AUD 3.2m) to be provided **after** Completion. DL 3 confirms it is not repaid and no discharge is in hand.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The full payout figure, including interest and break costs, treated as Indebtedness and paid at Completion from the purchase price through the funds flow.
  - A signed payout letter before Completion, and a deed of release plus PPSR discharges (including any share security) delivered **at** Completion.
  - A specific indemnity for any residual amounts.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** *Reason: the deal is debt-free/cash-free. Change of control under DD-003 clause 8.1 may trigger default, and post-Completion release leaves security over an asset the Buyer has paid for.*

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 in DD-005 Completion bonuses is "a matter for the Seller" and is not itemised in the funds flow. DL 5 is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Bonuses plus all employer on-costs (payroll tax, super guarantee, workers' comp, PAYG compliance) defined as Transaction Expenses or Indebtedness and deducted from the price.
  - Payment through Company payroll at or immediately after Completion, funded by the Seller.
  - A specific indemnity, outside the cap and basket, covering amounts that crystallise later under the continued-employment conditions.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the Seller position; require a price deduction plus an indemnity.** *Reason: the Company, not the Seller, is the legal payer. Without a funds-flow line item, the Buyer effectively pays at least about AUD 420k extra after the price is settled.*

## Specific Risks

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The existing indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment (DD-010: AUD 180,000 open) and is "considered adequate". DL 4 confirms no proof of payment and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **As a CP or Completion deliverable:** evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees, plus a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay (and moral rights consents where relevant).
  - **A broad specific indemnity** covering third-party IP claims, the loss of or inability to use the SOW3 Project Materials, and remediation and re-development costs. This should sit outside the cap, basket and disclosure, with a time limit of at least 3–6 years.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as inadequate.** *Reason: under DD-004 clause 7.3, title to the Project Materials does not pass until every fee is paid. The risk is losing core product IP, not a AUD 180k debt.*

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material. DL 6 discloses about 1,240 records sent by link to an unintended external address, with access, scope and notifiability all unresolved.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Pre-Completion covenants:**
    - complete the eligible-data-breach assessment under the Privacy Act Notifiable Data Breaches scheme;
    - obtain an independent forensic report, including link access logs and revocation;
    - make any required OAIC and individual notifications;
    - share all correspondence with the Buyer.
  - **A specific indemnity** for regulatory penalties, notification and remediation costs, third-party claims and customer credits. This should sit outside the cap, basket, disclosure and knowledge qualifiers, ideally backed by an escrow or retention.
  - Warranty that no other incidents have occurred.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "not material" characterisation; require an indemnity plus covenants.** *Reason: the Act generally expects assessment within 30 days. The matter was still "preliminary" at 22 September and it is now November, which itself creates compliance exposure. The penalty regime has been significantly increased.*

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 total) are "ordinary-course operating costs". DL 8 says to read DD-008 and DD-011 together, and does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Full copies of the renewals, plus confirmation of approval authority and any internal thresholds.
  - Treatment as non-ordinary course requiring Buyer consent under the conduct-of-business clause.
  - If they were entered without that consent, or are not terminable without cost: either (a) termination before Completion at the Seller's cost, or (b) treatment as Leakage or debt-like items deducted from the price, or covered by a specific indemnity.
  - Related-party and contract-splitting warranties.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the "ordinary course" label; investigate and reserve.** *Reason: three identical AUD 110k related renewals look like a single AUD 330k commitment split to stay under an approval or disclosure threshold.*

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced" by the share register at DD-012. DL 10 itself notes the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Buyer-side verification: current ASIC company extract and historical share issues, constitution, all issue and transfer documents, share certificates, a PPSR search over the shares, and a check for options, convertibles, ESOP or other rights to shares.
  - A warranty of 100% legal and beneficial title free of Encumbrances, under the fundamental regime in SPA-N-004.
  - **At Completion:** signed transfers, original certificates (or a lost-certificate indemnity), resignations, and releases of any security over the shares (link to Riverlark).
- **Recommendation:** **Do not rely on the register alone.** *Reason: a share register is only prima facie evidence. Riverlark security or unrecorded equity rights could defeat 100% title.*

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP positions are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Tax:** a separate tax indemnity or deed covering pre-Completion tax (including payroll tax and super on the bonuses), with Buyer conduct of tax claims, outside the general cap and basket, running for the statutory period plus 6 months.
  - **IP:** detailed IP warranties covering ownership and assignments from employees and contractors (including Ironquay), open-source compliance, no infringement, and data and privacy compliance. Title-to-IP elements should be treated as quasi-fundamental.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "settled"; table full tax and IP terms in our mark-up.** *Reason: in a SaaS acquisition, tax and IP are core value drivers. Folding them into a 20% / 18-month / data room-disclosed regime leaves them effectively unprotected.*

## Other Points (Not Itemised Above)

- **Office lease (DD-007):** Confirm the notification obligation is given at or before Completion, and the Seller warrants that no landlord consent is required.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** Obtain legal confirmation that the assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale or change of control. If uncertain, seek a comfort letter.
- **DL 1.4 non-admission and DL 11 reservation:** Acceptable as non-admissions only. Ensure they do not dilute specific disclosure standards or indemnities.

## Suggested Next Steps

1. **Confirm internally** whether any principal-level agreement exists on cap, basket or time limits.
2. **Issue the Buyer mark-up,** leading with category separation (N-014), disclosure (N-006) and knowledge (N-007), since these determine whether every other protection works.
3. **Send a supplementary due diligence request** covering Bluefen consent drafts, the Riverlark payout figure, Ironquay payment evidence, the privacy forensic status, Sandbar contracts and title documents.
4. **If W&I insurance is contemplated,** align the policy exclusions so the known matters (N-008 to N-013) are covered by Seller indemnities or escrow, since W&I insurers will exclude known issues.

*This is a working analysis for the Buyer deal team and should be reviewed by supervising NSW counsel before it is sent to the Seller.*
